producer_report.summary: Raised [budget] job_usd in athena.toml from 8.00 to 12.00 (one line). Added the test the_repository_budget_covers_two_reading_and_two_planning_rounds in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs. It parses REPO_CONFIG (include_str! of athena.toml), asserts job_usd == 12.0, and asserts 2*reader_usd + 2*(planner_usd + critic_usd) + producer_usd + verifier_usd (9.00 today) is at most job_usd, with every cap read from the parsed config. Two existing tests hard-coded the old value and were updated: run_pin_tests.rs now replaces "job_usd = 12.00" (so the tight-budget test still tightens), and crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs asserts caps.run == 12.0 (a file the brief did not list; the plan named it and cargo test needs it). Added a Changed entry under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md.

checks_run.note: full suite; every test result line shows 0 failed. Ran twice because the first run's output was saved to a file I could not read.

criteria_check.criterion: athena.toml [budget] has job_usd = 12.00 and reader_usd = 0.50, producer_usd = 3.00, verifier_usd = 2.00 are unchanged; git diff of athena.toml shows only that one line changed.
criteria_check.evidence: Edited only the line job_usd = 8.00 to job_usd = 12.00 in athena.toml; no other line touched. Parsed by the new test, which passes.

open_issues: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs was edited although the brief's deliverables do not list it; the plan called for it and without it the suite fails.
mistakes: The first full `cargo test --locked` output was too large and went to an unreadable file, so I reran the suite with -q. That is two full runs, one more than the guidance.
learnings: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs the_default_plan_budget_affords_a_read_where_drain_would_need_a_read_and_a_run hard-codes the repository job_usd (caps.run) and had to move from 8.0 to 12.0.
crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs needs no change: it has no job_usd or 8.00.
Tool output saved to files under ~/.claude cannot be read with Grep or Read (outside the working directory), so use `cargo test -q` for compact output.
